The reading measure

Text lines stop at 68 characters, so the eye finds the next line without effort. Figures and tables use the full column of 960 pixels. A paragraph longer than four lines is a sign to cut words or move detail behind More.

Word budgets. Title at most 8 words. Lede one sentence of at most 25. A card at most 40 words of body.

Decisions

Each decision answers in one word. Your picks build one reply line to copy into chat.

TPF-D3

A product with no image

Waits on you

TikTok and Pinterest refuse a product with no image. 38 of 2,512 products in Aster Home have none.

Trade-offs 4 points
  • O1: the channel never shows a broken product
  • O1: the blocked list says what to fix
  • O2: TikTok rejects placeholders after review
  • O2: the product looks unfinished to shoppers

Recommended O1. Google and Meta already work this way, so the store sees one rule.

TPF-D4

When the feeds refresh

Waits on you

Both channels read the feed URL on their own schedule. We choose how often it is rebuilt.

Recommended O2. Stock changes reach both channels within minutes, at no extra cost.

Sales channels screen

Detail on click

The page shows the summary. More, Tabs, Drill and Term hold the rest, one click or tap away.

More

Evidence 4 sources
  • TikTok Catalog product fields, the official spec
  • Pinterest catalog data source format
  • Our Google feed build, feeds/google.py
  • Aster Home catalogue, 2,512 products
Why the sale price is dropped for Pinterest

Pinterest reads sale price only with a start and end date. Our catalogue has no dates, so a sale price would be refused for every product.

Tabs

31 fields, 9 required. Images at least 500 by 500 pixels. Reads the feed URL every hour.

27 fields, 7 required. No sale price without dates. Reads the feed URL once a day.

A work document

Four groups in the sidebar, always in this order, each with as many pages as the work needs.

GroupWhenWhat it holds
OverviewAlways, firstStatus and stage, what waits on you, what changed, the versions
ResearchWhen neededWhat was found before designing: sources, today's behaviour
DesignAlwaysHow it works, screens, tables, open decisions; its last page is the issue
VerificationAlwaysThe checks, the tests to add, the PR and the tester results
